label: COMMUNICATION

cover.headline: When he’s stressed: *support him without carrying it*
cover.sub: 5 ways to help and still stay steady.

points.heading: Ask what kind of help he wants
points.body: Some people want solutions. Some want to vent. Ask before you fix.
points.panel: “Do you want ideas, or do you just want me to listen?”

points.heading: Listen without taking it on
points.body: You can care about his stress without making it yours to solve.

points.heading: Don’t take his mood personally
points.body: A short answer after a hard day is often about the day, not you.
points.panel: Before reacting, ask yourself: is this about me, or about his day?

points.heading: Offer one practical thing
points.body: A small lift can mean more than a big talk.
points.panel: “I’ll handle bedtime tonight. Go take a breather.”

points.heading: Keep your own calm
points.body: Your steadiness helps more than matching his worry.
points.panel: Take a walk or call a friend when you need to reset.

close.save: Save this for a stressful week.

caption:
When someone we love is under pressure, it’s easy to soak it all up, or to feel shut out by it.

There’s a middle path: being a steady, caring presence without carrying everything yourself. Here are five ways to do that. You don’t need all five. Even one can make a heavy week feel lighter for both of you.
